ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Fruit fly somatic cells have 4 pairs of chromosomes, of which No. 2, No. 3, and No. 4 are autosomes. It is known that the gene controlling the long-wing/vestigial-wing trait is located on chromosome No. 2, and the gene controlling the gray-body/ebony-body trait is located on chromosome No. 3. A group crossed an eyeless gray-body long-wing female fly with an eyed gray-body long-wing male fly. The phenotypes and proportions of the hybrid offspring are shown in the table. Answer the question: If the gene controlling the eyed/eyeless trait is located on chromosome No. 4, and gray-body long-wing eyed homozygotes are crossed with ebony-body vestigial-wing eyeless homozygotes, after the F1 intercross, there are 8 phenotypes in both females and males in F2, when the eyeless trait is a recessive trait. What is the proportion of ebony-body long-wing eyeless individuals in F2?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image table shows: Offspring are divided by eye trait into eyed and eyeless categories, each marked as 1/2; under the eyed and eyeless categories, they are further divided by sex into female and male, each marked as 1/2; within each eye-trait and sex group, the ratio of gray body long wing : gray body vestigial wing : ebony body long wing : ebony body vestigial wing is 9:3:3:1. The hypothesis states that the long-wing/vestigial-wing gene is on autosome No. 2, and the gray-body/ebony-body gene is on autosome No. 3; if the eyed/eyeless gene is on autosome No. 4, and eyeless is recessive, then the three pairs of genes are located on different autosomes and are inherited independently. Suppose gray body, long wing, and eyed are controlled by dominant alleles B, V, and E respectively, and ebony body, vestigial wing, and eyeless are b, v, and e respectively. The cross between gray-body long-wing eyed homozygotes and ebony-body vestigial-wing eyeless homozygotes, namely BBVVEE × bbvvee, produces F1 all as BbVvEe. When F1 intercross to obtain F2, the probability of ebony body bb is 1/4, the probability of long wing V_ is 3/4, and the probability of eyeless ee is 1/4. The three are independent, so multiplying gives the proportion of ebony-body long-wing eyeless individuals in F2 as 1/4 × 3/4 × 1/4 = 3/64.
